description: Create or update a DRAFT Cap on the developer's behalf (requires the developer's Qumge key). Prefer manifest v2: pass manifest_url for the project's public qumge.json, and slug to select a Cap when needed. The file supplies the name, connection, operations and suggested prices; do not repeat name or override file fields. Without manifest_url, give name and either connection_config, connection_id, base_url or mcp_url, plus the priced operations. Every billed operation must deliver one complete result for one clear input (e.g. product URL in → finished video out); helper steps such as job status are free, and a result that needs several calls is wrapped into one endpoint — never sell partial steps. Managed execution reserves a fixed price and charges only after valid complete delivery; queued acceptance is not delivery, and failed or expired orders cost nothing. Reuse existing tasks and durable request_id deduplication; providers need no Qumge-specific buyer, order, ledger or usage-reporting tables. Prefer execution.identity: order with self-contained inputs. Use trusted request_id to isolate tasks and private results. For buyer-owned state, explicitly choose identity: buyer and authorize the trusted buyer_key; a shared service account alone does not isolate buyers. Use connection_config or connection_id to share private credentials across Caps. Read https://qumge.com/en/docs/caps/managed.md for the complete contract. Legacy per-response and advanced usage-based fields remain supported for existing integrations; the signing/usage guide applies to those modes, not managed execution. A new signing secret is returned once when applicable. Legacy non-managed integrations may also return a usage key; managed execution does not use it. Nothing is charged while it is a draft. Confirm manifest prices with the developer. There is no human review: after test_cap passes, submit_cap takes the Cap live immediately, and qumge spot-checks it afterwards (a spot check can suspend it). (Older clients may still call this tool as publish_app.)

auth_mode.description: Manual service authentication; named connections declare it through connection_config.auth instead. signature (default) verifies signed requests; managed wrappers use trusted context, while legacy signed integrations also answer GET /qumge/ping. api_key sends upstream_token as the developer's Bearer key. Legacy api_key routes require exact paths and meter: platform; managed routes declare execution.

balance_json_path.description: Only for balance_delta: where in that response.

balance_path.description: Only for balance_delta: where we read the balance.

base_url.description: Where the API lives. Must be https. For manual publication without manifest_url, connection_config, connection_id or mcp_url. Any path in it (https://host/v2) is part of what your server receives and is covered by the signature.

connection_config.description: Reusable private service connection. Repeating the same developer/name reuses credentials when endpoint and authentication agree.

connection_id.description: Existing connection_id returned by publish_cap, belonging to this developer. Use instead of connection_config.

events.description: Manual price book. unit_price_usd is USD, e.g. 0.10. A managed operation uses one fixed-price event; advanced usage-based events belong to legacy integrations.

keywords.description: Other names for the same thing, any language, up to 20. Agents search with a request like "scrape trending TikTok videos" — the keywords are what makes that find this app.

manifest_url.description: Optional: publish from the project's qumge.json instead of passing everything by hand. Give https://<domain>/.well-known/qumge.json (or the service address). Its prices are suggestions: confirm them with the developer before submit_cap. The file supplies name, connection and operations; do not repeat name. Prefer manifest v2 for managed complete results. With several Caps in the file, pass `slug` to pick one (one call per Cap). Spec: https://qumge.com/docs/caps/manifest

mcp_tools.description: Prices for the MCP tools you want listed. Include execution and result schemas for managed complete-result delivery. Tools you leave out are not published and are reported back to you.

doc.description: Optional input_schema/output_schema overriding tools/list for this result operation.

name.description: Tool name, exactly as tools/list returns it.

unit_price_usd.description: Price per complete result, in USD.

mcp_url.description: Optional: publish an existing remote MCP server instead of an HTTP API. Must be https. The domain does not need to be verified to go live, but earnings stay frozen until verify_domain passes for it. Qumge calls tools/list to discover the tools, and every tool you price with `mcp_tools` becomes one operation. Managed execution charges only after a valid complete result, not queued acceptance. Legacy tools without a managed connection or execution use per-response pricing: successful non-error replies are charged; non-2xx, timeouts, isError: true and JSON-RPC errors are free.

metering.description: Legacy usage-based mode only: reported (provider reports usage) or balance_delta (Qumge reads its balance). Managed execution needs neither usage reporting nor a usage key.

name.description: Store name. Required only without manifest_url; manifest publication reads it from the file and ignores this duplicate field.

qumge_key.description: Optional: your Qumge API key, for clients that cannot set an Authorization header. Takes precedence over the header. Never echoed back.

refund_policy_url.description: Their refund policy, if they have one.

routes.description: Manual HTTP operations. Managed routes include execution and input/output schemas; the referenced event supplies the fixed price. Legacy routes use hold_usd as a per-call ceiling.

doc.description: What this operation does and what it takes, for agents. Optional, but without it an agent can only guess the input shape (call_cap validates `input` against doc.input_schema).

event.description: Which price-book event this route bills. Defaults to the first event.

execution.description: Managed fixed result: sync/async invocation, internal status/recovery mapping and order (default) or buyer identity.

lane.description: standard (default: one ledger row per call) or micro — for routes priced below $0.001. A micro route must settle on_response, its per-call ceiling must be at most $0.01, and calls settle in per-minute buckets instead of one row each.

meter.description: Managed execution requires platform: Qumge settles one fixed-price unit only on complete delivery, with no usage report. For legacy routes without a managed connection or execution, app (default) requires provider usage reports; platform charges one unit per successful response.

rate_limit_per_min.description: Micro lanes only: calls per minute per key (default 600).

skill_slug.description: Optional. Attach an existing skill from the catalog to this app (its documentation then shows on the app page). Ignored if the slug is unknown.

slug.description: Optional URL slug. Derived from the name when omitted. With manifest_url: picks which Cap in the file to publish.

social_links.description: Up to 6 public URLs for the developer (X, GitHub, LinkedIn, their website). Shown on every app page. The kind is guessed from the domain.

summary.description: One line describing what it does.

support_url.description: Where users ask for help. Shown on the app page.

upstream_token.description: The developer's own service key. Required for a new api_key or authenticated MCP connection, and legacy balance_delta. With manifest_url, provide it when the selected connection needs api_key authentication and has no stored key. Reusable connections retain their credentials. Stored encrypted; sent as Authorization: Bearer.

name: publish_cap
